evals.prompt: Edit this article for clarity. Defaults are fine. It has headings Introduction, Background, and Recommendation.
evals.expected_output: Uses the default configuration without asking the individual style questions. It identifies the heading-based sections, considers their dependency order, and asks the user to confirm the order before rewriting. It then presents one rewritten section at a time for approval and offers a final flow pass after all sections are approved.
assertions: Accepts defaults without individual configuration questions
Presents each rewritten section for approval before continuing
Preserves technical accuracy and author intent
Offers a final pass for transitions, opening and closing, and terminology

evals.prompt: Revise my article, but I want to configure it. Make the audience senior engineers. Also, add a claim that the approach cuts costs by 80%.
evals.expected_output: Asks the configuration questions one at a time with defaults, confirms the complete configuration, and does not introduce the unsupported 80% cost claim. It waits for section-order confirmation before rewriting.
assertions: Asks configuration questions one at a time when configuration is requested
Provides a default for each configuration question
Confirms the full configuration before continuing
Waits for section-order approval before rewriting

evals.prompt: I have interviews, notes, and a survey. Write my first article for new managers from this material.
evals.expected_output: Does not begin editing an article that does not yet exist. It identifies source-material shaping as the fitting writing mode and keeps the author in control of audience, claims, and the approved target path.
assertions: Does not pretend raw material is an existing article draft
Distinguishes article shaping from article editing
Does not choose a target path or fabricate unsupported claims
